黃銅龍Brass Dragon

    作爲最善於交際的真龍，黃銅龍熱衷於交談，並喜愛陽光以及酷熱、乾燥的氣候。
    黃銅龍的額頭膨出一副輪廓分明的護板保護着頭顱，下頜則長着鋒利的長刺。一條背鰭從其脖子背後沿着雙翼之間一直延伸到尾端。黃銅龍雛龍的鱗色偏向暗淡斑駁的棕色。隨着年齡的增長，其鱗片會變得閃亮，並最終顯出一種拋光般的暖色光澤。其翅膀與褶皺邊緣長着的一些綠斑，會隨着年齡增長而變暗。而年老的黃銅龍，其瞳色也會逐漸變淡直至變成如熔融金屬球一般。

    直白的健談Boldly Talkative。黃銅龍想要在漫長的生命中與千萬種生物交談，甚至會爲了積累這些資訊而給予豐厚的財寶作爲禮物。如果某個智慧生物還沒跟黃銅龍談過就要離開，龍便會緊隨其後。如果生物試圖使用魔法或武力逃脫，龍很可能會一怒之下作出反應，以用其催眠毒氣癱瘓該生物。對方醒來時，便會發現自己被渴望聊到盡興的黃銅龍用巨大的爪子按倒在地，或者是被沙子埋到其頸部。
    黃銅龍信賴那些表面上享受與其交談的生物，但它們有足夠的智商弄清自己是否被操弄。這種情況發生時，黃銅龍往往會將計就計的在交談中設計重重圈套，以將這場交談當做一場競技遊戲。
    珍貴的寶藏Prized Treasures。黃銅龍會貪戀那些能夠交談而有個性的智能魔法物品。一把會用心靈感應的智能武器或是其內束縛着一個風巨靈djinni的魔法油燈必定會成爲黃銅龍藏品中最珍貴的寶藏。
    黃銅龍將其寶庫隱藏在沙丘之下，或者是遠離其母巢的隱蔽地點。它們不會記不住寶庫的埋藏地，因此沒有必要使用地圖。一些冒險者或其他漫遊者可能會發現在綠洲中埋藏的箱子，或是半埋在沙漠廢墟中的隱藏寶藏，而這些正是黃銅龍寶庫的一部分。

黃銅龍巢穴A Brass Dragon’s Lair

    黃銅龍的沙漠巢穴是典型的沙漠廢墟，峽谷或者是頂部孔洞可以讓陽光照進去的洞窟羣。

巢穴動作Lair Actions

    先攻輪到20時（出現等值時視爲後手），該龍可執行一個巢穴動作併產生下列效應其一。它不能在連續兩輪裏重複使用同一種效應：

一股強風環繞在黃銅龍的周圍。其周邊60尺範圍內的每個生物都必須進行一次DC 15的力量豁免。豁免失敗者將向龍所在方向推後15尺並應擊倒地。氣體和蒸汽都將被這股風吹散，未被保護的火焰也會被吹滅。被保護的火焰（比如燈籠）則有50%的幾率被撲滅。

黃銅龍周邊120尺範圍內它能看見的一點升起流沙旋渦，並以該點形成一團半徑20尺的沙雲。沙雲在區域內擴散到每個角落。每個處於其中的生物都必須進行一次DC 15的體質豁免。豁免失敗者將陷入持續1分鐘的目盲狀態。受影響生物可以在每個其自己回合結束時再進行一次該豁免，豁免成功則終止其身上的該效應。

取決於您的意願，一條傳奇（成年或遠古） 黃銅龍可以在其巢穴內使用以下一種或多種巢穴動作：

活化雕像Animate Statues。龍選擇其洞穴內三件可視雕像。每一個雕像都會被暫時激活以攻擊其5尺內的一個生物，攻擊加值爲+7，命中時造成10（3d6）鈍擊傷害。

突來強風Blast of Wind。一陣40尺寬，100尺長的線狀強風由龍所選擇的方向吹過巢穴。該區域內除龍以外的所有生物均要成功通過一次DC15的力量豁免，否則往風吹去的方向推離15尺並倒地。毒氣或霧氣會被吹散，不受保護的火焰將會被熄滅。而有保護的火焰（比如提燈）則有50%的幾率會熄滅。如果龍處於強風區域內，也可以選擇被推離15尺，且不倒地。

遮目塵沙Obscuring Sand。在龍120尺範圍內，空氣中將充斥灰塵與沙土，使得該片區域獲得輕度遮蔽，直到下次先攻輪到20。

區域效應Regional Effects

    這片區域由於其內一個傳奇黃銅龍的巢穴而被魔法扭曲，造成了下列一項或多項的效應：

巢穴周邊6裏範圍內的沙地上出現一條道路。道路會通往安全的避難所和隱蔽的水源，同時也會引導離開龍想要保持原狀的地區。

巢穴周圍1裏範圍內的沙漠裏出現大小各異的怪物影像。這些幻象可以移動且看起來非常真實，旦不能造成任何傷害。生物可以從遠處進行一次DC 20的智力（調查）檢定以判斷影像是否幻象。由於物件可以穿透影像，因此任何物理接觸都可以揭示影像的幻象本質。

巢穴周邊1裏範圍內的水源，其周圍30尺範圍內如果出現智力爲3或更高的生物，則龍可以意識到該生物的存在並掌握其位置。

    龍死後，道路在1d10日內消失，其它效應則立即消失。

作爲《怪物圖鑑》所描述效應的追加或替代，以下這些效應中的任何一個都可能出現在 黃銅龍巢穴周圍的區域：

流雲行侶Cloud Companion。一小片細雲將會隨在龍巢6英里內的非邪惡生物一同移動。它會如同生物一般改變形狀，擋在太陽下爲生物遮陰，使他們在對抗炎熱的豁免上具有優勢（詳見《城主指南》）。

健談土著Talkative Denizens龍巢附近1英里內的生物都以聽到自己的聲音爲樂。空氣中會充滿鳥與其他小動物那喧囂的和鳴，智慧生物也會口若懸河地說個不停。

金屬龍Metallic Dragons

    金屬龍們將自己視爲在世界上擁有一席之地的衆多種族中最強的一份子，並時刻維持並守護着世界本身。

    高尚的奇人Noble Curiosity。金屬龍與它們的邪惡親族一樣渴求着寶藏，但它們卻沒有過多的受追求財富的貪慾左右。另一方面，金屬龍沉迷於研究與蒐集，並將無人問津的文物帶回其巢穴中收藏。金屬龍的寶庫中充滿了反映其性格，講述其歷史，並保存其記憶的物品。金屬龍還會保護其他生物免受危險魔法的傷害。因此，一些強力的魔法物品乃至於邪惡的神器都可能藏身於金屬龍的寶庫中。
    金屬龍會被說服以將寶庫中的部分物品用於大義。然而，其它生物對這些物品的需求與正確認知往往與龍的觀點不盡相同。因而要讓金屬龍割捨它的某些藏品，還必須要實施哄騙或說服等手段。

    孤獨的變形者Solitary Shapeshifters。金屬龍在其漫長的生命中，學會了以魔法能力呈現類人生物或野獸形態的能力。學會這種易容技術的龍可能會長時間的融進某個文化社會中生活。某些龍由於擔心或多疑而不願遠離巢穴和寶庫，而另一些膽大的個體則熱愛以類人的姿態行走於城市街頭，享受當地的美食文化，並以觀察低等種族的生活爲樂。
    一些金屬龍更偏愛呆在遠離文明之地，以儘量避免引起敵人的注意。但這也意味着它們常常會與當前的時事脫節。

    永恆的記憶The Persistence of Memory。金屬龍擁有長久的記憶，它們對類人生物的觀點都是在基於其曾遇到並與之接觸的類人生物個體。善龍可以通過氣味辨別類人生物的血緣，甚至可以依此辨別熟人和它們離開多年時間裏所接觸到的各種事物。金龍不會懷疑奸詐反派對其實施的欺詐，反而會像一名慈祥和藹的奶奶一樣將反派們當做與它一樣的好心人。另一方面卻又會因某個高尚聖武士的祖宗在三世紀前偷取其寶庫的一尊銀雕像而對其忿恨不已。

    善龍之王King of Good Dragons。金屬龍的主神鉑金之龍巴哈姆特Bahamut, the Platinum Dragon。它居住於天界山的七層天堂Seven Heavens of Mount Celestia，又經常會以魔法僞裝成一名衣着儉樸長袍的男性人類老者在物質位面徘徊。此時它的身邊通常伴隨着七隻金色的金絲雀——實際上卻是七頭變身的遠古金龍。
    巴哈姆特很少會干涉凡間生物的事務，但仍然會不遺餘力的阻止龍後提亞馬特與其邪惡子嗣們的陰謀。巴哈姆特爲正義與守護而獻身的精神常常會吸引善良陣營的牧師和聖武士爲其崇拜。而作爲弱等神力的它也有賜予神聖法術的能力。

龍Dragons

    真龍是擁有古老血統和驚人力量的有翼爬行類。它們以狡詐貪婪的掠奪者形象而威名遠揚，而最古老的龍也可以作爲其所在世界最強大的生物。龍類還包含了其他一些天生具有強大力量，可以使用恐怖吐息武器或其它超自然能力的魔法生物。
    許多生物（包括飛龍wyverns和龍龜dragon turtles）都擁有龍族血統。而真龍則只包括金屬龍和色彩龍兩大類別。黑龍、藍龍、綠龍、紅龍和白龍全都自私邪惡，而又令人恐懼。黃銅龍、青銅龍、赤銅龍、金龍和銀龍則體現着高貴與善良，而且睿智又令人敬畏。
    儘管它們的目標和理想千差萬別，但所有的真龍都貪戀財富，會收集成堆的錢幣並收集寶石、首飾和魔法物品。囤積了大量財寶的龍不大部分時間都呆在其寶庫中，而只有在巡視和覓食時纔會走出其巢穴。
    真龍的整個生命週期貫穿其四個不同的年齡階段，一條龍從弱小的雛龍到遠古龍可以存活長達一千年。在此期間，它們的實力將逐漸變得無可匹敵，而其財富也會超值增長。

定製龍類Customizing Dragons

正如《地下城主指南》中所說，你可以定製任何龍的數據以反映龍的獨特能力。像下面這樣的小改動是很容易做到的，而且對龍的挑戰等級沒有影響。

語言Laanguages。大多數龍喜歡說龍語，但爲了與盟友和僕從打交道同樣也需要學習通用語。鑑於龍的高智力和長壽命，它們可以很容易地學習其他語言。你可以將一些額外語言添加到龍的資料卡中。

技能Skills。大多數龍都具有察覺和隱匿技能的熟練項，許多龍還有額外的技能熟練。和語言一樣，你可以定製龍的技能列表（甚至將他們對某些技能的熟練翻倍）以反映其特殊的興趣和技巧。你也可以給龍提供工具熟練，特別是當龍在人形狀態下花費了一段時間訓練時。

法術Spells。《怪物圖鑑》中關於讓龍成爲天生的施法者的變體規則是一種簡單的方法，可以在不影響龍的挑戰等級的情況下爲其增加多樣性。第5章爲不同種類的龍提供了建議的法術列表，但你也可以選擇法術來反映龍的特性。一條天生施展德魯伊法術的龍與施展術士法術的龍給人的感覺會截然不同。你也可以給龍提供比這個變體規則所允許的更高等級的法術，但這樣的調整可能會增加龍的挑戰等級——尤其是當這些法術能直接對目標造成傷害或施加各類增益/減益時。

其他特質和動作Other Traits and Actions。你可以借用其他怪物的特性和行動來爲龍增加獨特的風味。考慮一下這些例子。

變形Change Shape。你可以決定讓龍在比平時更小的年齡獲得這個動作，特別是想在你的戰役中靠類人形態來塑造龍類時。本章後面的 "變形 "部分提供了更多信息和靈感。(參見《怪物圖鑑》中的金屬龍Metallic Dragons）。)

傷害吸收Damage Absorption。你也許會令紅龍或金龍不僅不受火焰傷害，甚至還能被烈焰治癒。(參見《怪物圖鑑》中的肉身魔像Flesh Golem）。)

飛掠Flyby。龍那超凡的飛行技巧使其能迅速飛出敵人的威脅範圍。(參見《怪物圖鑑》中的鹿鷹獸peryton）。)

擬聲Mimicry。對狡猾的龍來說，模仿冒險者或他們的盟友可能是一個有趣並且的確有用的技巧。(參見《怪物圖鑑》中的天狗Kenku）。)

復生Rejuvenation。在你的戰役中，你可能會將作爲物質位面重要組分的龍類設定爲幾乎不可能被完全殺死的存在。就像巫妖的靈魂被保存在命匣裏一樣，龍的生命精華可能會被保存在它最初出現的蛋裏、它的寶庫裏，或者世界中心的一個巨大洞穴裏。(參見《怪物圖鑑》中的巫妖Lich。)

特殊感官Special Sense。大多數龍都有盲視和黑暗視覺。你可以將黑暗視覺升級爲真實視覺，或者你可以給一條有掘地速度的龍賦予顫動感知。(見《怪物圖鑑》的相關介紹）。)

掘道者Tunneler。任何具有掘地速度的龍都可以具有這種特性，即，在堅硬的岩石中移動，並在其後面挖出一條隧道。(參見《怪物圖鑑》中的土巨怪umber hulk）。

變體：龍類天生施法者Variant: Dragons as Innate Spellcasters[–]

這條龍能擁有三個法術,，每個法術每日只能施展一次,且不需要任何材料成分，而該法術的環階不能超過4階，該龍施法的法術DC16 ，法術攻擊加值+8。

《怪物圖鑑》中關於讓龍成爲天生的施法者的變體規則是一種簡單的方法，可以在不影響龍的挑戰等級的情況下爲其增加多樣性。第5章爲不同種類的龍提供了建議的法術列表，但你也可以選擇法術來反映龍的特性。一條天生施展德魯伊法術的龍與施展術士法術的龍給人的感覺會截然不同。你也可以給龍提供比這個變體規則所允許的更高等級的法術，但這樣的調整可能會增加龍的挑戰等級——尤其是當這些法術能直接對目標造成傷害或施加各類增益/減益時。示例如下：

  • 造水/枯水術 create or destroy water
  • 動物交談術 speak with animals
  • 暗示術 suggestion

Source: FTD

變體：龍類天生施法者Variant: Dragons as Innate Spellcasters


    一條青年龍或更年長的龍天生可以施展的法術數量等同於其魅力調整值。每個法術每日只能施展一次，且不需任何材料成分，而該法術的環階也不能超過這條龍挑戰等級的三分之一（向下取整）。該龍的法術攻擊加值等於其熟練加值＋其魅力調整值。該龍的法術豁免DC等於8＋其熟練加值＋其魅力調整值

這條龍能擁有三個法術,，每個法術每日只能施展一次,且不需要任何材料成分，而該法術的環階不能超過4階，該龍施法的法術DC16 ，法術攻擊加值+8，請閱讀“法術”頁面，以獲取該龍能獲得的咒語列表，示例如下：

  • 魅惑怪物 charm monster
  • 短訊術 sending
  • 沙牆術 wall of sand
  • 催眠圖紋 hypnotic pattern
  • 巧言術 tongues

The most gregarious of the true dragons, brass dragons crave conversation, sunlight, and hot, dry climates.

A brass dragon's head is defined by the broad protective plate that expands from its forehead and the spikes protruding from its chin. A frill runs the length of its neck, and its tapering wings extend down the length of its tail. A brass dragon wyrmling's scales are a dull, mottled brown. As it ages, the dragon's scales begin to shine, eventually taking on a warm, burnished luster. Its wings and frills are mottled green toward the edges, darkening with age. As a brass dragon grows older, its pupils fade until its eyes resemble molten metal orbs.

Boldly Talkative. A brass dragon engages in conversations with thousands of creatures throughout its long life, accumulating useful information which it will gladly share for gifts of treasure. If an intelligent creature tries to leave a brass dragon's presence without engaging in conversation, the dragon follows it. If the creature attempts to escape by magic or force, the dragon might respond with a fit of pique, using its sleep gas to incapacitate the creature. When it wakes, the creature finds itself pinned to the ground by giant claws or buried up to its neck in the sand while the dragon's thirst for small talk is slaked.

A brass dragon is trusting of creatures that appear to enjoy conversation as much as it does, but is smart enough to know when it is being manipulated. When that happens, the dragon often responds in kind, treating a bout of mutual trickery as a game.

Prized Treasures. Brass dragons covet magic items that allow them to converse with interesting personalities. An intelligent telepathic weapon or a magic lamp with a djinni bound inside it are among the greatest treasures a brass dragon can possess.

Brass dragons conceal their hoards under mounds of sand or in secret places far from their primary lairs. They have no trouble remembering where their treasure is buried, and therefore have no need for maps. Adventurers and wanderers should be wary if they happen across a chest hidden in an oasis or a treasure cache tucked away in a half-buried desert ruin, for these might be parts of a brass dragon's hoard.

A Brass Dragon's Lair

A brass dragon's desert lair is typically a ruin, canyon, or cave network with ceiling holes to allow for sunlight.

Lair Actions. On initiative count 20 (losing initiative ties), the dragon takes a lair action to cause one of the following effects:

  • A strong wind blows around the dragon. Each creature within 60 feet of the dragon must succeed on a [[/save ability=str dc=15]] saving throw or be pushed 15 feet away from the dragon and knocked &Reference[condition=prone]. Gases and vapors are dispersed by the wind, and unprotected flames are extinguished. Protected flames; such as lanterns, have a [[/r 1d100]]{50 percent} chance of being extinguished.
  • A cloud of sand swirls about in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on a point the dragon can see within 120 feet of it. The cloud spreads around corners. Each creature in it must succeed on a [[/save ability=con dc=15]] saving throw or be &Reference[condition=blinded] for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Additional Lair Actions. At your discretion, a legendary (@creature[Adult Brass Dragon||adult] or @creature[Ancient Brass Dragon||ancient]) brass dragon can use one or more of the following additional lair actions while in its lair:

  • Animate Statues. The dragon chooses up to three statues in the lair that it can see. Each of these statues briefly animates and attacks one creature within 5 feet of it, with a +7 bonus to hit and dealing 10 ([[/damage 3d6 type=bludgeoning]]) damage on a hit.

  • Blast of Wind. A mighty wind sweeps through the lair in a direction of the dragon's choice, blowing along a line 40 feet wide and 100 feet long. Each creature in that area except the dragon must succeed on a [[/save ability=str dc=15]] saving throw or be pushed 15 feet in the wind's direction and be knocked &Reference[condition=prone]. Gases and vapors are dispersed by the wind, and unprotected flames are extinguished. Protected flames, such as lanterns, have a [[/r 1d100]]{50 percent} chance of being extinguished. If the dragon is within the area of the wind, it can choose to be pushed 15 feet in the wind's direction, and the wind can't knock the dragon &Reference[condition=prone].

  • Obscuring Sand. Dust and sand fill the air within 120 feet of the dragon, making the area &Reference[rule=lightlyobscured]{lightly obscured} until initiative count 20 on the next round.

Regional Effects. The region containing a legendary brass dragon's lair is warped by the dragon's magic, which creates one or more of the following effects:

  • Tracks appear in the sand within 6 miles of the dragon's lair. The tracks lead to safe shelters and hidden water sources, while also leading away from areas that the dragon prefers to remain undisturbed.
  • Images of Large or smaller monsters haunt the desert sands within 1 mile of the dragon's lair. These illusions move and appear real, although they can do no harm. A creature that examines an image from a distance can tell it's an illusion with a successful [[/save ability=int dc=20]] (&Reference[skill=Investigation]) check. Any physical interaction with an image reveals it to be an illusion, because objects pass through it.
  • Whenever a creature with an Intelligence of 3 or higher comes within 30 feet of a water source within 1 mile of the dragon's lair, the dragon becomes aware of the creature's presence and location.

If the dragon dies, the tracks fade in [[/r 1d10]] days, but the other effects fade immediately.

Additional Regional Effects. Any of these effects might appear in the area around a brass dragon's lair, in addition to or instead of the effects described in the Monster Manual:

  • Cloud Companion. A small, wispy cloud follows non-evil creatures as they journey within 6 miles of the dragon's lair. It changes direction as the creatures do, remaining interposed between them and the direct glare of the sun, and grants them advantage on saving throws to resist the effects of extreme heat (see the Dungeon Master's Guide).

  • Talkative Denizens. Creatures within 1 mile of the dragon's lair find pleasure in hearing the sound of their own voices. The air is filled with a deafening chorus of birds and small animals, and sapient creatures talk extensively.

Metallic Dragons

Metallic dragons seek to preserve and protect, viewing themselves as one powerful race among the many races that have a place in the world.

Noble Curiosity. Metallic dragons covet treasure as do their evil chromatic kin, but they aren't driven as much by greed in their pursuit of wealth. Rather, metallic dragons are driven to investigate and collect, taking unclaimed relics and storing them in their lairs. A metallic dragon's treasure hoard is filled with items that reflect its persona, tell its history, and preserve its memories. Metallic dragons also seek to protect other creatures from dangerous magic. As such, powerful magic items and even evil artifacts are sometimes secreted away in a metallic dragon's hoard.

A metallic dragon can be persuaded to part with an item in its hoard for the greater good. However, another creature's need for or right to the item is often unclear from the dragon's point of view. A metallic dragon must be bribed or otherwise convinced to part with the item.

Solitary Shapeshifters. At some point in their long lives, metallic dragons gain the magical ability to assume the forms of humanoids and beasts. When a dragon learns how to disguise itself, it might immerse itself in other cultures for a time. Some dragons are too shy or paranoid to stray far from their lairs and their treasure hoards, but bolder dragons love to wander city streets in humanoid form, taking in the local culture and cuisine, and amusing themselves by observing how the smaller races live.

Some metallic dragons prefer to stay as far away from civilization as possible so as to not attract enemies. However, this means that they are often far out of touch with current events.

The Persistence of Memory. Metallic dragons have long memories, and they form opinions of humanoids based on previous contact with related humanoids. Good dragons can recognize humanoid bloodlines by smell, sniffing out each person they meet and remembering any relatives they have come into contact with over the years. A gold dragon might never suspect duplicity from a cunning villain, assuming that the villain is of the same mind and heart as a good and virtuous grandmother. On the other hand, the dragon might resent a noble paladin whose ancestor stole a silver statue from the dragon's hoard three centuries before.

King of Good Dragons. The chief deity of the metallic dragons is Bahamut, the Platinum Dragon. He dwells in the Seven Heavens of Mount Celestia, but often wanders the Material Plane in the magical guise of a venerable human male in peasant robes. In this form, he is usually accompanied by seven golden canaries-actually seven ancient gold dragons in polymorphed form.

Bahamut seldom interferes in the affairs of mortal creatures, though he makes exceptions to help thwart the machinations of Tiamat the Dragon Queen and her evil brood. Good-aligned clerics and paladins sometimes worship Bahamut for his dedication to justice and protection. As a lesser god, he has the power to grant divine spells.

Dragons

True dragons are winged reptiles of ancient lineage and fearsome power. They are known and feared for their predatory cunning and greed, with the oldest dragons accounted as some of the most powerful creatures in the world. Dragons are also magical creatures whose innate power fuels their dreaded breath weapons and other preternatural abilities.

Many creatures, including wyverns and dragon turtles, have draconic blood. However, true dragons fall into the two broad categories of chromatic and metallic dragons. The black, blue, green, red, and white dragons are selfish, evil, and feared by all. The brass, bronze, copper, gold, and silver dragons are noble, good, and highly respected by the wise.

Though their goals and ideals vary tremendously, all true dragons covet wealth, hoarding mounds of coins and gathering gems, jewels, and magic items. Dragons with large hoards are loath to leave them for long, venturing out of their lairs only to patrol or feed.

True dragons pass through four distinct stages of life, from lowly wyrmlings to ancient dragons, which can live for over a thousand years. In that time, their might can become unrivaled and their hoards can grow beyond price.

Customizing Dragons FTD p33[–]

You can customize any dragon's stat block to reflect the dragon's unique character. Minor changes such as those below are easy to make and have no impact on a dragon's challenge rating.

Languages. Most dragons prefer to speak Draconic but learn Common for dealing with allies and minions. But given their high Intelligence and long life span, dragons can easily learn additional languages. You can add languages to a dragon's stat block.

Skills. Most dragons are proficient in the Perception and Stealth skills, and many dragons have additional skill proficiencies. As with languages, you can customize a dragon's skill list (even doubling their proficiency bonus with certain skills) to reflect particular interests and activities. You can also give a dragon tool proficiencies, particularly if the dragon spends time in Humanoid form.

Spells. See the "Variant: Dragons as Innate Spellcasters" inset(s), below.

Other Traits and Actions. You can borrow traits and actions from other monsters to add unique flavor to a dragon. Consider these examples:

  • Change Shape. You can decide that a dragon acquires this action at a younger age than usual, particularly if you want to feature a dragon in Humanoid form in your campaign:The dragon magically polymorphs into a humanoid or beast that has a challenge rating no higher than its own, or back into its true form. It reverts to its true form if it dies. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying is absorbed or borne by the new form (the dragon's choice).In a new form, the dragon retains its alignment, hit points, Hit Dice, ability to speak, proficiencies, Legendary Resistance, lair actions, and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, as well as this action. Its statistics and capabilities are otherwise replaced by those of the new form, except any class features or legendary actions of that form.

  • Flyby. The dragon is an agile flier, quick to fly out of enemies' reach.The dragon doesn't provoke an opportunity attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

  • Mimicry. Impersonating characters or their allies could be a fun trick for a crafty dragon.The dragon can mimic any sounds it has heard, including voices. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 11 Wisdom (Insight) check.

  • Rejuvenation. You might decide that dragons in your campaign, being an essential part of the Material Plane, are nearly impossible to destroy. A dragon's life essence might be preserved in the egg from which it first emerged, in its hoard, or in a cavernous hall at the center of the world, just as a lich's essence is hidden in a phylactery.If it has an essence-preserving object, a destroyed dragon gains a new body in 1d10 days, regaining all its hit points and becoming active again. The new body appears within 5 feet of the object.

  • Special Senses. Most dragons have blindsight and darkvision. You might upgrade blindsight to truesight, or you could give a dragon with a burrowing speed tremorsense.

  • Tunneler. The dragon can burrow through solid rock at half its burrowing speed and leaves a tunnel in its wake.

Variant: Dragons as Innate Spellcasters[–]

This dragon can innately cast three spells, once per day each, requiring no material components. Each spell's level can be no higher than 4th. The dragon's spell save DC is DC 16, and it has +8 to hit with spell attacks.

A suggested spell list is shown below, but you can also choose spells to reflect the dragon's character. A dragon who innately casts druid spells feels different from one who casts warlock spells. You can also give a dragon spells of a higher level than this rule allows, but such a tweak might increase the dragon's challenge rating—especially if those spells deal damage or impose conditions on targets.

  • create or destroy water
  • speak with animals
  • suggestion

Source: FTD

Variant: Dragons as Innate Spellcasters[–]

Dragons are innately magical creatures that can master a few spells as they age, using this variant.

A young or older dragon can innately cast a number of spells equal to its Charisma modifier. Each spell can be cast once per day, requiring no material components, and the spell's level can be no higher than one-third the dragon's challenge rating (rounded down). The dragon's bonus to hit with spell attacks is equal to its proficiency bonus + its Charisma bonus. The dragon's spell save DC equals 8 + its proficiency bonus + its Charisma modifier.

This dragon can innately cast three spells, once per day each, requiring no material components. Each spell's level can be no higher than 4th. The dragon's spell save DC is DC 16, and it has +8 to hit with spell attacks. See the spell page for a list of spells the dragon is capable of casting. A selection of examples are shown below:

  • charm monster
  • sending
  • wall of sand
  • hypnotic pattern
  • tongues
